plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: Silvery-green mounds send up slender spikes crowded with tiny, fragrant, violet-blue flowers. The blooms hum with bees and perfume the warm air of the French countryside.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late June to August in Provence, with the first blooms opening in mid-June
plants.funFact: The name comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash'. Romans scented their baths with lavender.

plants.name: Paeonia lactiflora
plants.description: Ruffled, bowl-shaped blooms as large as a saucer unfurl on sturdy stems above glossy, deeply cut leaves. They bring a lush, sweet fragrance to cool-climate gardens and wild mountain meadows.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late May to mid-June in northern temperate regions
plants.location: Northern China, Mongolia and Siberia, plus gardens across northern Europe and North America
plants.funFact: Peonies have been cultivated in China for more than 1,500 years. Some plants can live and bloom for over a century.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A dramatic flower head the size of a dinner plate, with a crown of silky pink bracts around a soft, downy center. It is South Africa's national flower and thrives on fynbos hillsides.
plants.bloomingSeason: Peak from late winter to spring in the Southern Hemisphere, with flowering from about May to November
plants.funFact: Proteas are among the oldest flowering plants on Earth. The genus is named for the Greek god Proteus, who could change his shape.
